land.text: 'Around 1200 BC, the Hittite kings Tudhaliya IV and Suppiluliuma II waged military campaigns in Alashiya and forced its king to sign a treaty of submission'

successors.note: The page does not say whether Alashiya survived as a vassal; the hittites dossier (me-04-a) lists Tudhaliya IV's temporary annexation of Cyprus as not drawn.

capitals.name: Enkomi (possible)
capitals.note: The page says the capital 'may have started at Enkomi, or may have always been at Kalavasos'; the Enkomi page opened is the modern town and gives no history. Coordinates are those of Famagusta, the nearest gazetteer place, approximate.

correction.text: Alashiya, 'Cyprus, in whole or in part'; the page calls it unclear whether the kingdom covered all of Cyprus or only part (copper provenance points to Kalavasos and Alassa in the south)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Alashiya (the Greek Dark Ages and Cyprus Condominium rows are later and cover Cyprus differently). The page says it is 'unclear' whether the kingdom was all of Cyprus or part of it and gives no area; the island (about 7,600 km2 of land in the gazetteer) is the maximal reading and the keyframe should be treated as soft.

region.text: Alashiya, 'Cyprus, in whole or in part'; the page calls it unclear whether the kingdom covered all of Cyprus or only part (copper provenance points to Kalavasos and Alassa in the south)

ledger.note: c. 1400 BC (first dated mention): Alashiya is a land of its own. 'Around 1400 BC, the Hittite king Arnuwanda I chastised his vassal Madduwatta for raiding Alashiya.' The page gives no founding year and says only 'Middle and Late Bronze Ages'; the start is a bridging judgment at this earliest dated sentence. The Amarna letters (c. 1350 BC) have its king calling the Pharaoh 'brother' and sending copper.

ledger.note: c. 1200 BC: Alashiya submits to Hatti. 'Around 1200 BC, the Hittite kings Tudhaliya IV and Suppiluliuma II waged military campaigns in Alashiya and forced its king to sign a treaty of submission'; the Tudhaliya IV page has 'a statue was set up by Tudhaliya IV to commemorate his conquest of the Land of Alasiya' (reign c. 1245-1215 BC) and dates the tablet CTH 121 to Suppiluliuma II (c. 1210-1185 BC). Neither page says whether a king stayed.

notes: Cliopatria has no Alashiya; the 'Greek Dark Ages' row (-1100..-801) is the only Cyprus shape near the era. The Alashiya page is thin: no infobox, no founding, no extent, no end. Every date here is the Hittite-side or Amarna-side mention, so the 1400 start and the 1200 end are bridges at confidence 1-2, the whole island is a maximal reading and the capital is a placeholder. The fate of Cyprus after the Hittite campaigns (the kingdoms of the Iron Age, Kition, Salamis; the Sea Peoples and Enkomi's end) is not on any page opened; a gap-filler should open 'Ancient Cyprus' or 'Enkomi' (the English title may differ) and 'Kition'. Kition (c. 900-310 BC) is in me-04-a's counterparts list. Page budget: three pages, one of them empty.
